text:
omar: flagging a weird race: we applied a temporary runtime pin to na-east-small for stability but deploy-bot shows a scheduled rollback from an older change window that would remove the pin in ~20m. Need to coordinate so we don't flip-flop. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: [info] pinlist: na-east-small runtime-pin:runtime@3.2.0-stable applied by omar at 1799991120 (id=pin-20240605-01). Scheduled rollback task in queue: rollback-job-442 (trigger at 1799992450) created by release-manager-late.

ivy: where did the scheduled rollback come from? I didn't schedule anything.

sre-oncall: I see a legacy automation job that clears temporary pins after 2h automatically. It picked up an older change-id and scheduled rollback. That will conflict with our hotpatch.

paul: recommendation: pause the automation job and mark the pin as "hold-for-hotpatch". Then we can unpause and remove hold once validated. Commands: `/deploy pinlist hold pin-20240605-01 --reason "hotpatch in progress"` and to resume: `/deploy pinlist release-hold pin-20240605-01`.

qa-bot: current smoke on na-east-small: api_surface PASS, perf PASS, model_bind PASS, error-rate 0.02% sampled 5000 requests. link: https://ci.redwood/internal/testruns/na-east/4102

omar: agreed. Please pause automation and add hold. I'll kick off final hotpatch build and smoke. If smoke stays green for 30m we remove the pin and clear the scheduled rollback job.

deploy-bot: action queued: add-hold -> target=pin-20240605-01, requested_by=omar, runbook_ref=/runbooks/pin-hold-procedure.md

release-manager: that scheduled rollback was created as part of nightly cleanup. Sorry for the noise; I can cancel it once you confirm hold.

deploy-bot: [completed] hold applied to pin-20240605-01 at 1799991367 by omar. Scheduled rollback job rollback-job-442 canceled.

sre-oncall: documented change window: start=1799991120, hold_applied=1799991367, expected unhold after validation. change-id=chg-20240605-pin-hold. Notifying automation owners.

omar: thanks. starting hotpatch build now. Will post results. If anyone sees abnormal telemetry ping me directly. :thumbsup:
